content: 1. The World Health Organization (WHO) has published guidelines aimed at preventing early pregnancies and poor reproductive outcomes among adolescents in developing countries. These guidelines were accessed on January 30, 2018. 2. A document titled From Evidence to Policy: Expanding Access to Family Planning was reviewed, providing insights into improving family planning services. This document was accessed on January 30, 2018. 3. A framework has been developed to ensure human rights are upheld in the provision of contraceptive information and services. This framework was accessed on January 30, 2018. 4. The United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) and WHO have created an implementation guide to ensure human rights are integrated into contraceptive service delivery. This guide was accessed on January 30, 2018. 5. WHO has issued a guideline on implementing effective actions to improve adolescent nutrition. This guideline was accessed on January 30, 2018. 6. A review titled Adolescent Pregnancy: Unmet Needs and Undone Deeds examines literature and programmatic issues related to adolescent health and development. This review was accessed on January 30, 2018. 7. A fact sheet on family planning and contraception is available on the WHO Media Centre website. This resource was accessed on January 30, 2018. 8. The International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO) has issued recommendations on adolescent, preconception, and maternal nutrition under the theme Think Nutrition First. These recommendations were published in the International Journal of Gynecology and Obstetrics in 2015. 9. Research by Casanueva et al. (2006) highlights that adolescents with adequate birth weight newborns reduce energy expenditure and cease growth. This study was published in the Journal of Nutrition. 10. A study by Rah et al. (2008) in rural Bangladesh found that pregnancy and lactation negatively impact the growth and nutritional status of adolescent girls. This research was published in the Journal of Nutrition. 11. Rah (2013) provided an opinion piece discussing the impact of adolescent pregnancy on the growth and nutritional status of young mothers, based on available evidence. This was published in Sight and Life. 12. Wallace et al. (2004) explored how nutritional factors mediate placental growth restriction in growing adolescents and its consequences for the fetus. This study was published in Biology of Reproduction. 13. WHO has issued recommendations on health promotion interventions for maternal and newborn health. These recommendations were accessed on January 30, 2018. 14. WHO has also provided guidelines on antenatal care to ensure a positive pregnancy experience. These guidelines were accessed on January 30, 2018. 15. A guideline on vitamin A supplementation during pregnancy to reduce the risk of mother-to-child transmission of HIV was reviewed. This guideline was accessed on January 30, 2018. 16. A global assessment by Prüss-Üstün et al. (2016) evaluates the burden of disease caused by environmental risks and emphasizes the importance of healthy environments. This report was published by WHO. 17. WHO has published a report on the cost and cost-effectiveness of water quality interventions to prevent diarrheal diseases. This report was accessed on January 30, 2018. 18. Prüss-Üstün et al. (2008) authored a report titled Safer Water, Better Health, which was accessed on January 30, 2018. 19. WHO has issued a guideline on preventive chemotherapy to control soil-transmitted helminth infections in at-risk populations. This guideline was accessed on January 30, 2018. 20. WHO emphasizes the importance of the physical school environment as a key component of health-promoting schools. This report was published in 2004. 21. A document titled Local Action: Creating Health-Promoting Schools was reviewed. This document was accessed on January 30, 2018. 22. Adams et al. (2009) published a report on water, sanitation, and hygiene standards for schools in low-cost settings. This report was published by WHO. 23. WHO has issued global recommendations on physical activity for health. These recommendations were accessed on January 30, 2018. 24. A document titled Promoting Physical Activity in Schools highlights the importance of physical activity as part of health-promoting schools. This document was accessed on January 30, 2018. 25. WHO published a guide titled Making Health Services Adolescent Friendly in 2012, which was accessed on January 30, 2018. 26. A report titled Adolescent-Friendly Health Services: An Agenda for Change was reviewed. This report was accessed on January 30, 2018. 27. WHO and UNAIDS have developed global standards for quality health-care services for adolescents, including an implementation guide. This guide was accessed on January 30, 2018. 28. McKee et al. (2000) discussed the UNICEF experience in involving people and evolving behavior in a publication titled Involving People, Evolving Behavior. 29. Alderman et al. (2013) published a report on improving nutrition through multisectoral approaches. This report was published by the World Bank Group. 30. Garrett and Natalicchio (2011) authored a report on working multisectorally in nutrition, including principles, practices, and case studies. This report was published by the International Food Policy Research Institute. 31. WHO and UNFPA have provided technical guidance for prioritizing adolescent health. This guidance was accessed on January 30, 2018. 32. WHO has developed implementation tools for essential noncommunicable disease interventions in primary health care settings with limited resources. These tools were accessed on January 30, 2018. 33. WHO's global report on preventing chronic diseases emphasizes the importance of investing in prevention. This report was accessed on January 30, 2018. 34. Epping-Jordan et al. (2005) discussed stepwise actions for preventing chronic diseases in a publication in The Lancet. 35. Snowdon et al. (2008) proposed a practical approach using problem and solution trees to identify potential interventions for improving population nutrition. This study was published in Health Promotion International. 36. Swinburn et al. (1999) developed a framework for identifying and prioritizing environmental interventions for obesity. This study was published in Preventive Medicine. 37. WHO has published a guide on health program evaluation, providing principles for its application in national health development. This guide was accessed on January 30, 2018. 38. A WHO document on monitoring, evaluation, and review of national health strategies emphasizes a country-led platform for information and accountability. This document was accessed on January 30, 2018. 39. WHO's Global Database on the Implementation of Nutrition Action (GINA) provides information on nutrition interventions. This database was accessed on January 30, 2018.
